reading_rule: Complete selected scientific source values, with custody-only fields removed as documented. Author-state tokens remain dated source history; original later qualification governs scientific acceptance.

common.F004_forward: The particular state/history representation below exposes an ordering or history distinction that actually changes the native inference. Its transition/event/observation semantics are part of the premise; no state-machine notation is compulsory and a static relation or equation can remain sufficient for a narrower subquestion.
common.F004_reverse: The native temporal distinction identifies the state, events, history and observations the representation must retain. It determines when a stateless table is adequate and when erasing order would lose the intended claim; it does not prove the model corresponds to an implementation or physical process.
common.F005_forward: The named state predicate is an actual local safety/accounting or evidence-preservation obligation of this native model/computation. A sound reachable-state proof or completed exploration can establish it; sampled assertions support only their observed states. This partial invariant does not establish every temporal, statistical or mission claim.
common.F005_reverse: The native function/accounting requirement identifies the consequential invariant and its exact domain. A passing assertion for a weaker field or a different quantity is insufficient; a direct finite test or human proof can still be proportionate.
common.F006_forward: For the specified state predicate, prove initiation and consecution over the actual admitted transitions, and implication to the needed native subclaim. This is a valid way to discharge that obligation, not a claim that the displayed candidate is already inductive or that a failed induction proves a reachable counterexample.
common.F006_reverse: The native state/accounting obligation selects the candidate invariant, relevant initialization and transition cases. It exposes omitted alias, fault, observation or time changes. The intended predicate may need strengthening or a different proof, with no arbitrary exclusion of relevant states.
common.F007_forward: The member-specific classification separates the safety, progress, terminating-computation or quantitative obligations that actually occur in this use. A total contract can establish finite-function result and termination together; no taxonomy is imposed where a direct contract already suffices.
common.F007_reverse: The actual native objective selects which state/trace/computation property is required and which stronger implication would be needed to reuse a different kind of evidence. It does not itself establish safety, progress, fairness or a quantitative bound.
common.F008_forward: The stated eligible action/progress use can receive a conditional fairness input, or a concrete limit on a proposed fairness-based inference. Weak/strong fairness concerns continuously/repeatedly enabled actions, not missing eligibility, physical availability, exact diagnostic accuracy or a finite deadline.
common.F008_reverse: The specific native action identity, enabling condition and intended eventual/deadline result determine which fairness assumption, if any, is relevant. They expose when a stable intention is lost behind fresh attempts, when a resource is absent, and when an explicit bounded-response premise is needed.
common.fairness_control: Already executed NX03 and its analytic extension distinguish stable intention from fresh attempts and qualitative fairness from delays beyond a deadline. In a model where an action remains enabled, scheduling it at any finite time tau greater than d and then continuing fairly gives a fair execution missing deadline d. No finite response bound follows merely from weak or strong fairness. This construction is not a probability model.
common.negative_forward: After examining the actual supplied calculation, safety/history predicate and partial evidence uses, no scheduling/eligible-action progress obligation is present in this selected use. Fairness therefore supplies no identified input to that inference. The reason is not that it fails to establish the entire native property.
common.negative_reverse: The selected native static predicate or calculation provides no actual scheduler/enabling/progress premise for F008. A later concrete asynchronously scheduled diagnostic/control/analysis procedure may create such a use, but an arbitrary future worker or wrapper is not credited here.
common.negative_scope: Bounded to the exact inspected use and predicate, not every conceivable implementation or all future applications. Re-enter on a named action, enabling condition, scheduler semantics and consequential progress requirement. Ordinary terminating computations may require no fairness assumption.
common.physical_scope: Abstract resource/task states do not create physical access, skill, credential validity or action authority. The C07 alive/failed-by-mode process is a mathematical representation of the supplied independent constant competing hazards, not a newly run accelerated test. The HPP thinning/count model remains conditional on its actual stochastic assumptions.
common.cost_and_alternatives: Use the smallest adequate static table, direct algebra, total local contract, existing invariant or explicit scheduling bound. Count state/ghost-variable, proof, instrumentation and scheduling costs. A richer temporal model can expose a real distinction without being the cheapest production mechanism.
common.execution: Own author-exposed analytical mappings and deductions. Existing NX01/NX03/NX05/NX06/NX07, root r2/M3 and constituent C01-C14 retain their exact attribution. No new program, model checker or physical experiment is executed.

native_members.specific_temporal_or_nonmatch_argument: The actual comparison can contrast one enclosed local operation with remote send/accept/timeout/recovery histories. NX01 supplies the consequential uncertain-effect boundary introduced by the remote history; an invariant-only local requirement may still be met by a static/local contract.

Represent the proposed split with its shared-resource failure and recovery transitions. A single shared CPU/power transition can affect both deployments even when their names differ; the temporal path, rather than the deployment count, is the candidate isolation claim.

When the artifact is offered for the NX01/NX03 history-sensitive claim, its actual state/event model must retain the consequential timeout, stable intention or progress distinction. A static document/label cannot replace that distinction; a static adequate predicate remains valid for a different need.

The mission predicate may require the function throughout a named interval, so failure and restoration order matters even for equal end states. A finite event/mission trace represents that particular requirement, without redefining every mission as continuous success.

An operational profile that includes sequences/duty cycles must distinguish a clustered burst from the same calls separated by recovery. The exact supplied scenario partition can include those histories; frequency weights alone do not preserve their ordering effect or estimate their real prevalence.

The actual diagnostic profile includes detection latency. Fault onset, observation and alarm transitions distinguish detection within the required window from a later alarm even when the eventual detected count is equal.

For a sequential diagnostic test, update the candidate-cause set after each specified symptom/test result. The observation history can distinguish causes sharing the initial symptom; a sufficient remedy can still precede unique diagnosis.

Represent the selected detection-to-action path with alarm, eligibility, action and its modeled effect, keeping the supplied zero-delay M3 calculation as a simpler special case. The C10 capacity qualification changes whether the action can occur in its claimed useful window; the model does not estimate costs or efficacy.

The actual repair task has access, retained-state transfer, replacement/reassembly and validation prerequisites. Their order matters to feasibility; a task-transition model makes that ordering explicit without supplying physical access or measuring maintainability.

Support prerequisites become available or unavailable over the required repair window. Modeling information/credential, spare, skill and scheduling state distinguishes eventual eligibility from timely supported action; inventory alone is not processing headroom.

In the own HPP ascertainment derivation, true count N and observed count K have distinct event histories. Under independent detection q, a true failure increments N and increments K only if detected; this exposes why a zero observed history need not mean no true event. The Poisson/thinning law remains an explicit model premise.

The supplied C07 competing constant hazards admit states alive, failed-by-A and failed-by-B with the corresponding use/test transition intensities. Stress changes the two mode intensities by factors 10 and 2; the resulting mixture cannot be replaced by a single factor merely because the mode labels are unchanged.

Process events and exposure within their configuration/stratum history, retaining changes of configuration and missing-observation context. The update state distinguishes adding exposure from observing no failure; complete processing does not establish ascertainment or pooling validity.

The actual producer/consumer journey can require a later component only after a preceding postcondition. A transition/history model captures that sequence and the residual external dependency without erasing the useful first result or extending the chosen objective indefinitely.

For the chosen moving or fixed event window, record event entry/expiry and the selected response policy. A windowed ratio can change with time despite no new success event; a static C09 ratio remains adequate for its fixed-window counterexample.

The supplied probe/observer/capability model has an observation time and a later-use time. The same observed prefix can precede different later capability states, as in the received readiness controls; the transition relation supplies the currentness question.

For the NX01/NX03/NX05 consequential alternatives, use the smallest state/history model retaining the distinct effect, intention or preserved resource. This is an actual discriminator choice, not a requirement to express every simple calculation temporally.

Represent the shared sensor, scheduler or resource event that can affect both nominally diverse mechanisms. The common transition is a concrete dependence path; two state-variable names do not remove it or supply a calibrated joint law.

C01 describes 100 short outages versus one long outage over the same horizon. Their time histories have equal aggregate availability and different interruption consequences; a state trace retains the distinction that the scalar mean discards.

The declared event/window question can depend on outage placement or cohort-specific service histories. Preserve that actual interval/population in the trace before aggregating; a full trace calculation still does not choose acceptable stakeholder harm.

Use the actual C07 illustrative alive/failed-by-mode transition model as a partial input to the stated transfer comparison. This representation supplies no unread handbook coefficients or validation for a new technology; its physical intensities remain stipulated.

Where the worksheet claims protection against latent-plus-active failure sequences, model those actual transitions and control states. A populated static row can miss the order-dependent loss of the protection path; static mode analysis remains adequate for genuinely static questions.

Retain event and exposure accumulation with the before/after configuration intervals. C08 counts 10 to 5 with exposures 1000 to 100 then gives rates .01 to .05; the temporal/configuration record supports the denominator interpretation but does not identify a causal correction effect.

Separate the green/probe event from subsequent capability changes and unobserved paths. The actual observation trace can establish the narrow signal fact while a later/global-health claim needs an additional transition/currentness argument.

The deterministic branch can exclude a specific bad transition/state over an explicitly finite admitted model. The statistical branch counts observed events over exposure. Keeping those histories distinct prevents a finite model exclusion from becoming arbitrary-world zero risk.

The bounded automated controller has observation, allowed-action and restoration transitions. That explicit control fragment can be analyzed without claiming faithful arbitrary learned task semantics, beneficial field intervention or autonomous authority.
The modeled state remains within the admitted fault/timing/storage envelope at each protocol step; any extra failure action must be included rather than excluded to make induction pass.

Across the fixed current-state reset, the distinct past-effect histories in NX01 remain distinct even when current Q agrees. Preserve the relevant history/observation interpretation in the paired-state model; this is not an invariant asserting that later evidence can never resolve the past.

Within the admitted fault budget, each reachable state retains the required surviving-function predicate or its stated auxiliary protection invariant. A failed induction outside the fault budget is not an in-domain counterexample.

Recorded event clocks retain the selected causal-order relation as new events are added. Initialization, local increments and communication updates need the actual logical/vector-clock rules; physical time is a separate quantity.

Each completed admitted read satisfies the selected session/freshness condition relative to the preserved session context. Intermediate pending reads and legitimate later overwrites do not falsely count as violations of a previous return.

The incrementally admitted history retains the exact chosen consistency predicate or a stronger protocol invariant implying it. A true reachable history property may need auxiliary state rather than being inductive as written.

The enclosed runtime state preserves its intent/effect-accounting invariant through the admitted crash/replay steps. This can support the internal guarantee while leaving excluded effects and progress separate.
For the actual response interface, normal-returned implies the required local postcondition under the admitted precondition; pending and exceptional states have their own specified meanings.

The credited local closure flag/return is supported by the exact consumer postcondition at the relevant boundary. A wider unknown fact is not inserted as an invariant obligation when that consumer does not require it.

The retained probe record remains attached to its original capability/path/time interpretation. Later target transitions can invalidate a current-readiness extension without falsifying the narrower historical observation invariant.

After processing each actual retained-event prefix, aggregation counts and selection/context associations equal the defined aggregation of that prefix. This proves a computation/accounting facet, not representative sampling.

The graph-inference state contains only edges/relations justified by the observed edges and declared inference rules, with observed and inferred provenance retained. It does not establish completeness of physical causes.

Each recorded oracle outcome stays tied to the actual fault/hypothesis configuration and the intended discriminator. A constant pass or a wrongly linked scenario is a different predicate, even if record structure is valid.

The particular proposed local alternative preserves the actual enclosed invariant at each admitted operation. That partial functional result may remove a reason to distribute, without proving a global architecture optimum.

Each admitted removal/update step preserves the explicit residual consumer obligations, including required dormant protection. The supplied dependency relation remains a premise, not a proof that no unlisted future consumer exists.

Within the specified split/resource model, the protected function retains the actual resource condition under the admitted interference steps. Separate process names cannot be used as the inductive hypothesis for physical independence.

The selected NX05 protected-resource or other explicitly needed model predicate is the invariant the artifact must establish. Its usefulness comes from that consequential predicate, not from the presence of invariant syntax.

Each admitted agent protocol transition preserves stable intent/parameter binding and the bounded effect/recovery invariant. Open-ended task meaning and unsupported actions are outside this local result.

The selected admitted function states preserve the actual required-function predicate over the modeled mission steps. Its interpretation and interval remain explicit; a proxy state cannot replace the mission function.

The finite scenario-weight representation keeps nonnegative normalized weights and correct scenario association through its defined updates. Population correspondence and rare omitted scenarios remain separate from this necessary model-accounting invariant.

The already established local conjunct remains available at the next interface under the compatible state/frame assumptions. The invariant need not establish every still-open journey conjunct to be material.

In actual C01, after each iteration the processed outage record has down_hours=events*duration and availability=1-down_hours/horizon, while the other scenario keeps its meaning. This establishes the finite estimand computation, not a regenerative law.

Every retained finite joint-law candidate in NX07 obeys its nonnegativity, normalization and marginal constraints, and its success value uses the stated Boolean system function. Induction over the enumeration does not establish the separate all-real optimum/bound.

For the supplied C03/C12 diagnostic calculation, processed observation/outcome records retain the declared detection event and denominator; in C12 each emitted row obeys containment=detected AND safe_action. Calibration and actual fault latency remain separate premises.

A sound diagnostic-elimination step retains every candidate cause consistent with the observed history, including the true cause under the stated observation model. The set may remain non-singleton while an adequate remedy is available.

In root r2/M3, after each of the four world rows each policy loss equals the weighted loss sum over the processed prefix. This actual inner-loop invariant establishes the stipulated expected-loss input; action efficacy, zero delay and authority remain assumptions.

The repair-task model preserves required retained state/configuration and completes each prerequisite before dependent reassembly/validation. The invariant concerns task design; it does not supply physical access or measured repair time.

An admitted repair-dispatch state claims eligibility only when the stated support prerequisites and information/credential conditions are satisfied. A modeled eligibility invariant does not make those world predicates true or provide a finite scheduling deadline.

In the actual perfect age-replacement model, age starts at zero, increases only until the replacement/failure event and resets on genuine modeled renewal. The age-bounded cycle invariant is a policy-model premise, not a proof that resetting a software counter renews hardware.

An admitted condition-triggered action begins only under its actual threshold, remaining lead-time and resource preconditions. The invariant checks legal modeled initiation; it neither forbids relevant time passage artificially nor proves the action physically effective.

Failure/configuration identity and evidence linkage survive each allowed correction-status update. A Closed status can satisfy record consistency while the causal correction and later exposure remain unproved.

Under the declared no-false-positive thinning model, counts start N=K=0 and every true event increments N, with K incremented only for a detected event; thus 0<=K<=N through event steps. This supplies the actual count-model constraint without establishing q, HPP, ascertainment or a numerical confidence bound by itself.

In the supplied competing-risk model, each realization is alive or absorbed in exactly one failure mode; use/test rate labels remain attached to their mode. Event-step preservation of this state distinction supports the mixture definition without validating the physical acceleration law.

After each processed record, stratum/configuration event counts and exposure equal the defined prefix aggregates, with missing-observation flags retained. This is computational integrity, not unbiased ascertainment or valid pooling.

The corrected local software operation preserves the selected behavioral/resource invariant, as in the NX05 alias correction. The proof remains conditional on the operational input/state domain and does not supply a field failure probability.

The composed journey state retains the postconditions established by completed components until the next consumer uses them, under actual frame/compatibility conditions. Remaining external availability and later steps are separate.
The windowed event/cohort aggregation maintains the actual numerator/denominator and expiry rule. A correctly computed threshold state does not entail stakeholder acceptance or release authority.
The probe record continues to mean the specific observed capability at its recorded time; a later target-state change does not silently rewrite that observation into a present-health assertion.

NX05 preserves the actual useful observation resource through the disjoint reset, while the alias variant violates it. The induction step needs the true footprint/alias premise and supplies no crash durability or measurement truth.

The selected invariant must separate the actual alternatives, such as NX05 useful-resource preservation. A cheaper invariant about an irrelevant field or the C14 weak proxy does not become adequate merely because it is easy to prove.

A removal/replacement sequence retains the explicit residual control/evidence obligations and usable retained results. A theorem can stay true after active execution stops; changed premises require a different claim.

The bounded implementation/model preserves the actual no-shared-write or other specified structural separation condition through admitted changes. This can exclude a particular shared mechanism while leaving physical/common-input and probabilistic dependence open.

Actual C01 processes each separate outage record while preserving its distinct event count/duration and derived availability meaning. The equal-availability conclusion never becomes an invariant that the durations or distributions are equal.

The C01 computation preserves the declared time-window estimand while updating the two actual scenario records. The C09 cohort calculation keeps its own denominator; no invariant equates a passing aggregate with each subgroup succeeding.

The lifetime/process model keeps the relevant clock and quantity distinct through its admitted failure/renewal steps: age since genuine renewal is not automatically the same as calendar time or NHPP intensity. The chosen hazard curve remains an analytical/empirical premise.

The actual C07 competing-mode state and rate association are preserved through the represented failure events. This bounded model-accounting input does not validate handbook transfer, unread coefficients or a new population.

The finite mode/effect/control model preserves the actual protected-function predicate under the faults it claims to contain, or exposes a reachable failure state. A worksheet completeness invariant is not substituted for that control property.

The event/exposure computation keeps each count attached to its actual before/after exposure and configuration. Preserving this accounting distinguishes C08 rates .01 and .05; it does not establish causal improvement.

The policy model admits actions only with its stated feasibility/lead-time conditions and preserves the intended cost/accounting association. Correct policy-model state does not establish calibrated prediction, physical efficacy or universal policy superiority.

For one fixed U, the count-state relation n=floor(sqrt(t)+U) retains that same U across time and is nondecreasing. An event-step invariant must keep the shared latent variable; marginal mean matching or independent resampling does not supply the process law.

The deterministic branch uses the exact no-bad-state invariant within its admitted finite model. A statistical-bound calculation has a distinct interpretation; neither is promoted to an invariant of arbitrary physical worlds.

Every admitted action through the bounded automated interface preserves its specified critical-state/resource predicate. Unsupported generated commands, learned task fidelity, useful field outcomes and authority remain outside that invariant.

Surviving the admitted faults is a required-function safety/mission claim; eventual later repair alone is weaker than protection during the mission. A finite fault-function calculation can have a total contract of its own.
Rejecting a harmful stale mutation is a safety property. Eventual expiration, a fair scheduler or eventual new-holder access is not the same predicate.

The finite graph inference can be a terminating computation with a correct relation result. That total contract is distinct from eventual arrival of all missing events or a complete physical causal explanation.

The actual local/remote alternative may need an invariant and/or progress capability. Meeting one must not be used as the other; a terminating adequate local operation can combine its result and completion without temporal machinery.

Removal must preserve the actual residual safety and progress obligations that are specified. A remaining safe-but-inert mechanism can fail a required progress duty, while a dormant true theorem need not execute continuously.
The split may change a propagation/safety boundary or a required service-progress/capacity path. Those are separate consequences; separate deployment names establish neither.
Classify the exact artifact claim before crediting it to the consumer: a valid invariant proof is useful safety evidence but not automatically response progress or a field outcome.

A total scenario-weight calculation is distinct from representing the operational profile and from a temporal service-progress claim. The actual finite computation can be checked without pretending that termination calibrates its weights.
A contained-mode safety predicate and eventual recovery of function are different analysis claims. The finite mode/effect calculation can establish a bounded exclusion without asserting restoration.

The finite joint-law/system-function computation can be total and correct, while its probability weights remain supplied assumptions. A qualitative safety or eventual-recovery theorem alone does not determine that quantitative mission probability.

The added path must supply the stated conditional rescue, possibly within a mission interval. A safe unused spare or eventual switch after the interval is not the same function; the finite rescue calculation remains useful.

Correct candidate-cause exclusion is distinct from eventual diagnostic completion and from a successful remedy. A total finite symptom classifier can return a legitimate ambiguous set while an action-sufficient remedy is available.

A total correct expected-loss calculation is distinct from timely feasible execution of the chosen action. Neither diagnostic accuracy nor eventual response alone determines the stipulated policy utility.
Task-state preservation and eventual repair completion are distinct from a repair-time distribution. A finite task plan may establish order/safety without available support or a deadline.

Preserving unaffected state is a safety obligation; completing the intended maintenance change and validation is a separate progress/result obligation. A suitable total local contract can cover both its bounded result and termination.

The C05 numerical policy-cost computation can have a total result contract. Its result remains conditional on physical renewal/hazard/cost assumptions; eventual replacement and a preserved age bound do not establish those rates.
Record/linkage correctness, eventual closure of a work item and actual causal improvement are distinct. A terminating status update can be correct while the claimed correction remains unsupported.

Removing the modeled fault while preserving an invariant is a behavior/safety change; eventual deployment or faster completion is a different claim. A finite corrected helper can be proved total for its exact domain.

The C07 arithmetic is a finite terminating computation under its input domain. Correct total evaluation is a useful partial input but does not establish the physical stress-life mapping or a probability of timely failure by itself.

Correct finite aggregation and completion of processing differ from representative observations or future detection. A total update contract can establish the exact record result while leaving those statistical premises open.
Dependency/identity checking can be a total finite computation. That result determines affected evidence; it does not require continual rechecking or prove eventual arrival of new empirical support.

A graph/cut safety result or local assume/guarantee implication does not automatically establish eventual recovery through a dynamic dependency network. State the actual requested inference; a finite graph computation can be total.
Retirement can preserve a safety theorem yet remove a needed progress action, or stop redundant replay while preserving both. The actual residual requirement selects the distinction.

Structural diversity/separation evidence, eventual service and quantitative common-error probability are different propositions. A total dependency calculation can identify one shared mechanism without estimating its incidence.

Computing a stated hazard/cost function is a finite functional/termination question; the actual lifetime/process law is a mathematical or empirical model claim. Qualitative eventual failure does not specify the hazard shape.

Correctly terminating evaluation of the illustrative C07 transformation is a bounded computation result. It is distinct from handbook-model transfer accuracy, physical mechanisms and a policy consequence.
A reachable-state control exclusion and eventual restoration are different substantive failure-analysis results. Merely terminating worksheet processing or filling its fields establishes neither.
Conditional rescue must cover the declared function/interval; a safe added component or eventual activation can be too weak. The actual total finite rescue calculation remains a valid partial input.

The policy comparison can return the correct optimum among stipulated feasible choices and terminate. That does not establish future intervention progress, calibrated inputs or general predictive-policy superiority.

The count-process mean/law is quantitative. A nondecreasing count safety invariant or eventual occurrence of events does not identify NHPP increments; the finite marginal calculation has its own total-function scope.
The bounded controller may establish a safety invariant or a terminating local result while open-ended task completion, timely useful remediation and authority remain distinct.

An enabled remote commit/reply can occur before or after the timeout and still be part of a fair execution. Those two fair histories retain the consequential past-effect ambiguity; fairness alone does not retrospectively identify the effect at timeout.

If the proposed protection relies on asynchronously scheduled repair/switch actions, fairness can support eventual eligible execution but not survival through the stated mission deadline. The admitted late fair action is a concrete limit on replacing timely rescue with eventual recovery.

The convergence use requires the specified propagation/merge actions to occur; fair eligible delivery can support eventual convergence under the actual algorithm premises. It supplies no finite convergence time or separate invariant preservation.

When repeat erasure is claimed to preserve a required progress outcome, compare fairness on the stable intended action in the paired histories. Deleting or renaming the only enabling attempt can change that progress premise even when isolated f(f(x))=f(x) remains true.

A remote alternative offered for eventual service must state how its eligible request/recovery actions are scheduled. A fair conditional progress claim can be real, but it does not match a local bounded-response capability merely by being called reliable.

Removing a control can remove the enabling action needed by a residual progress obligation. A formerly fair conditional theorem is not falsified, but its premise/available action can cease to support the after-removal behavior.

For the split service whose progress depends on a shared scheduler, fair dispatch is a conditional eventuality premise. Both deployments can still suffer arbitrarily long fair delays, so a claimed isolation/latency benefit requires more than fairness or separate names.

The NX03 conditional progress theorem has a genuine bounded evidential role once its stable-action and fairness premises are named. It need not be discarded because it lacks a deadline, nor credited as a deadline theorem.

When comparing the local merge/coordination option with an amortized stronger service, preserve the actual delivery/scheduling progress contract. Fair eventual progress can suffice for one objective while an explicit bounded service is needed for another; less coordination alone does not choose that tradeoff.

A queued switch/repair action in the selected redundant path may be eventually scheduled under fairness if continuously enabled. Rescue before the mission deadline still needs a time bound and usable resource, and the added controller can fail.

If containment uses an asynchronously dispatched software intervention, fairness can support eventual dispatch only after its real enabling conditions hold. Containment before propagation reaches the protected function needs the separate timely-response premise.

A diagnostic action that remains enabled can eventually alarm under its stated fairness/coverage conditions. The native latency-qualified detection denominator is stricter: an arbitrarily late fair alarm can fail the required detection window.

For a sequential diagnostic procedure with a pending eligible discriminating test, fairness can support eventual performance of that test. It does not make the test informative, the cause unique or a physical probe available; an adequate immediate remedy may bypass it.

If the selected alarm response is dispatched asynchronously, a fairness premise may support eventual eligible action but cannot supply the M3 zero-delay or any finite useful-window assumption. The C10 capacity qualification remains necessary for a claimed feasible response.

For the finite repair task sequence, fair scheduling of actually enabled steps can support conditional eventual completion when the other termination/prerequisite premises hold. It creates neither access nor skill, and no maintainability-time bound follows.

The selected multi-step maintenance/validation procedure can require eventual scheduling of its enabled next step. Fairness supplies that limited progress premise while unaffected-state preservation and completion by a deadline remain separate.

The actual feedback process may have an eligible corrective/validation follow-up that must eventually be performed. A fair scheduling premise supports that process progress, not truth of the correction, its benefit or a deadline.

A dynamic recovery dependency path can progress only when its next required action is enabled. Fairness does not resolve a cycle in which no action becomes enabled, and a static reachability path alone does not establish that temporal premise.

For the actual NX03 progress/timeout alternatives, choose the stable-action fairness or explicit bounded-response discriminator that answers the objective. A correct fair eventuality theorem can be sufficient for the former and insufficient for the latter.

Retiring a control can remove a needed eligible progress action while retaining the truth of its old conditional theorem. The native removal question must preserve the real residual eventual/deadline obligation or a sufficient substitute.

Two diverse handlers sharing one delayed scheduler can both miss a finite deadline on an otherwise fair execution. This is a concrete shared timing-failure possibility, not a probability estimate or a claim that all diversity is ineffective.

A redundant path whose activation is an asynchronously scheduled action can be fairly activated after the protected mission has already failed. Conditional eventual activation is a useful but narrower premise than the claimed timely rescue.

For the specific zero-deadline-miss claim under only qualitative fairness, the admitted late fair execution is a counterexample. This narrows that proposed deterministic exclusion without denying a different valid bounded-model zero-bad-event theorem.

The bounded agent/controller protocol must attach fairness to the stable permitted task action and real enabling condition. Fairness can support that conditional progress, while fresh attempts, unavailable prerequisites, task semantics and action authority remain separate.

The inspected returned-read/session freshness predicate is conditional safety about the supplied history. It does not require that every pending read eventually return; adding such an availability objective would be a new receiving use.

The inspected linearizability/serializability/isolation predicate concerns admitted operation histories. A pending operation can be consistent without a progress guarantee; no actual scheduler fairness premise enters this history check.

The actual target is exclusion of a harmful accepted stale mutation. Fair or unfair scheduling does not establish the resource rejection guard, and no lock-acquisition progress claim is part of this inspected predicate.

The inspected invariant-confluence/update/merge closure question is a safety/algebraic relation over admitted states and operations. It does not demand eventual scheduling of an operation or delivery of a particular update.

The actual retained-event selection/aggregation calculation and missingness inference contain no scheduled next action. Eventual processing by an unspecified collector would not establish the supplied sampling assumptions.

The inspected finite graph/observed-edge relation can be evaluated as a terminating local computation. No promise that all missing events eventually arrive is supplied or required by that bounded inference.

The supplied finite fault/hypothesis/oracle discriminator has an explicit intervention domain. No asynchronous injection scheduler is part of this inspected experiment object; a later live injector may create a separate timing obligation.

The inspected integrated lock/resource protocol claim excludes the relevant stale-holder harm. Eventual acquisition or fair queuing is a different possible lock service property and is not used to establish this exclusion.

The selected finite scenario partition and weight interpretation are supplied model/profile data. Qualitative fair scheduling does not assign those weights or establish representative observation; no actual progress task is being proved.

The inspected finite mode/effect and control-coverage relation is static. Eventual execution of an imagined analysis worker would not fill an omitted failure mode or establish the represented control predicate.

The NX07 static joint-law constraints and threshold system-success calculation contain no asynchronous recovery scheduler. Fairness does not determine a joint distribution or the all-real probability bound.

The inspected C05 scalar renewal-cost comparison uses stated hazard/renewal/policy assumptions. It has no asynchronously scheduled software action whose fairness establishes physical renewal or the calculated policy cost.

The inspected changed mechanism/invariant removes a specified modeled fault path. Scheduling when a change is deployed is a different potential task; fairness does not prove correctness of the changed behavior in this use.

The C06/ascertainment inference is a probabilistic count/exposure calculation under explicit process and observation assumptions. It includes no scheduled diagnostic task; fairness cannot substitute for HPP, iid or q ascertainment.

The actual C07 use/test rate transformation is a finite scalar calculation under physical competing-hazard assumptions. Fair scheduling supplies neither the mode-specific acceleration law nor its parameter mapping.

The inspected fixed event/exposure/configuration aggregation and statistical interpretation use supplied records. No asynchronous collection or processing-progress contract is present; fairness cannot make missing observations representative.

The actual changed-premise/claim/identity dependency calculation is finite and can be synchronous. It does not require continual rechecking jobs or eventual new evidence, so no scheduler fairness condition participates.

The inspected fault/workload/oracle model and retained C12-style finite discriminator specify the intervention cases directly. No asynchronous injection/controller scheduler is supplied in this bounded use.

The NX05 question is preservation of the useful observation through a given reset. It is conditional on that operation, not a claim that a pending reset is eventually scheduled; fairness does not establish its footprint.

The inspected hazard/rate meaning and C05 scalar calculations have no scheduler/enabling action. Qualitative eventual failure or fair evaluation does not identify the lifetime/process law or curve shape.

The actual C07 illustrative transfer calculation and handbook-use criterion do not contain a scheduled progress action. Fairness supplies no coefficient provenance, physical mapping or finite arithmetic result.

The inspected substantive mode/effect/control relation behind the worksheet is a finite analysis object. No asynchronously scheduled protection action is provided in this use; fairness would not establish a missing mode or the control predicate merely by making analysis work eventually run.

The actual C08 count/exposure comparison is a supplied finite calculation. It does not include an asynchronously executed correction; fair future work scheduling would not establish this comparison or causal improvement.

The bounded supplied chaos hypothesis/fault/workload/oracle object has no asynchronous injector scheduler. A concrete live experiment with queued interventions could add a timing use, but it is not inferred from the chaos label.

The inspected finite predictive-policy comparison uses given feasibility, loss and intervention assumptions. No eligible-action scheduling theorem is supplied; fairness cannot establish calibrated predictions or the physical effects used in that comparison.
